title: movvar
summary: Compute moving variances in MATLAB and RunMat.

gpu_support.notes: GPU inputs currently use a resident fallback: gather once to host for the moving-window pass and re-upload the result when an acceleration provider is active.

description: `movvar(A,k)` computes variances over a sliding window of length `k` along the first non-singleton dimension.
behaviors: `k` may be a positive scalar window length or a two-element `[kb kf]` backward/forward window.
`movvar(A,k,0)` uses sample normalization by `N-1`, except singleton windows divide by `N`; this is the default.
Pass an explicit normalization flag before `dim`, for example `movvar(A,k,0,2)`, to move along a chosen dimension.
`'includenan'` is the default; `'omitnan'` and `'omitmissing'` skip NaN values inside each window.
`'Endpoints'` supports `'shrink'` (default), `'discard'`, `'fill'`, and numeric scalar fill values.
`'SamplePoints', sp` uses a strictly increasing numeric point vector for irregular moving windows. With sample points, RunMat currently supports shrink endpoints.
This implementation covers numeric, logical, complex, and gpuArray inputs; table/timetable `DataVariables` forms are tracked separately.
